subject: Assistance with Parallelizing the "modparcov" Function for Improved Execution Time

messages.author: f9de65b9184212be
messages.subject: Assistance with Parallelizing the "modparcov" Function for Improved Execution Time
parts:
Hi

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to seek your expertise and assistance with a programming challenge I am currently facing.
I have developed a function called "modparcov," which is crucial for my program's convergence. However, the execution time of this function
is significantly long, and I would like to optimize it for improved performance.
To address this issue, I have decided to run the program on a server with more than 20 cores. My intention is to parallelize the "modparcov" function,
allowing it to run concurrently and take advantage of the server's multiple cores. However, I am in need of guidance to achieve this parallelization effectively.

I would greatly appreciate it if you could provide assistance and guidance on how to parallelize the "modparcov" function. Specifically,
I am seeking advice on how to modify the code to ensure efficient utilization of the available cores and improve the overall execution time of my program.

If you have any suggestions, recommendations, or sample code snippets that demonstrate how to parallelize such functions effectively, please do share them
with me. Additionally, if there are any best practices or resources you could recommend for optimizing code execution through parallelization, I would be extremely grateful.
Thank you in advance for your time and assistance.
Your expertise and guidance will be of immense help in enhancing the performance of my program. I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Warm regards

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(spdep)
library(nimble)
library(GWmodel)


N <- S <- 211

data("baltimore")

y <- baltimore$PRICE

y <- matrix(y, nrow = length(y), ncol = length(y), byrow = FALSE)

x <- cbind(baltimore$DWELL,baltimore$NBATH,baltimore$PATIO,baltimore$FIREPL,
           baltimore$AC,baltimore$BMENT,baltimore$GAR,baltimore$CITCOU,baltimore$LOTSZ)

coords <- cbind(baltimore$X,baltimore$Y)

dist2 <- gw.dist(coords,focus=0,p=2,theta=0,longlat=F)

bw <- bw.gwr(PRICE~DWELL+NBATH+PATIO+FIREPL+AC+BMENT+GAR+CITCOU+LOTSZ,
             data=SpatialPointsDataFrame(coords,baltimore),approach="AIC",kernel="gaussian",
             adaptive=T,p=2,theta=0,longlat=F,dMat=dist2)


modparcov <- function(y, x, w) {
 
 
  # Main Function
  GWRCode <- nimbleCode({
    for (i in 1:S) {
      y[1:N, i] ~ dmnorm(mu_y[1:N, i], prec = tau_y0[1:N, 1:N, i])
     
      mu_y[1:N, i] <- b[i, 1] * x[, 1] + b[i, 2] * x[, 2] + b[i, 3] *
        x[, 3] + b[i, 4] * x[, 4] + b[i, 5] * x[, 5] + b[i, 6] * x[, 6] +
        b[i, 7] * x[, 7] + b[i, 8] * x[, 8] + b[i, 9] * x[, 9]
     
      tau_y0[1:N, 1:N, i] <- diag(psi_y[i] * exp(-Dist[1:N, i] / lambda))
     
      for (j in 1:9) {
        b[i, j] ~ dnorm(0, tau = tau_b[ind[j] + 1])
        ind[j] ~ dbern(gamma[j])
        tau_b[1] <- tau_b0
        tau_b[2] <- tau_b0 * c
        gamma[j] ~ dbeta(0.5, 0.5)
      }
     
     
     
      b0[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
      psi_y[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
    }
    lambda ~ dunif(0, D)
  })
 

  GWRData <- list(y = y, Dist = dist2, x = x)
  GWRConst <- list(S = S, N = N, D = 50, tau_b0 = 100, c = 0.0001)
  GWRInits <- list(psi_y = rep(1, GWRConst$S), ind = c(rep(1, 9)),
                   gamma = rep(0.5, 9), lambda = 10)
 
  # Run the Model
  mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code = GWRCode, data = GWRData, constants = GWRConst,
                         inits = GWRInits, thin = 1, niter = 10000, nchains = 1, nburnin = 5000,
                         monitors = c("b", "lambda"), setSeed = TRUE)
 
  # Posterior Convergence Diagnostics and Estimation
  library(coda)
  pos_mcmc <- as.mcmc(mcmc.out)
  beta <-pos_mcmc[, 1:1899]
 
  beta <- as.matrix(colMeans(matrix((pos_mcmc[, 1:1899]), N , 9)))
 
 
  sigma_y <- 1 / (mean(pos_mcmc[, 1900]))
 
  xpw <- t(x) %*% w
  invxpwx <- solve(xpw %*% x)
  c <- invxpwx %*% xpw
  varresid <- sigma_y
  ccp <- c %*% t(c)
 
  res <- list()
  res$par <- beta
  res$cov <- ccp * as.numeric(varresid)
  res
}

messages.subject: Re: Assistance with Parallelizing the "modparcov" Function for Improved Execution Time
parts:
Hi, could you say more about what specific part of the computation you're trying to parallelize? 

If you're trying to run multiple chains in parallel, we have information in this example on our website.

Also, one comment about efficiency: because your precision matrix, `tau_y0`, is diagonal, it's likely to be more efficient to just 
define the elements of `y[1:N, i]` as scalar nodes following the `dnorm` distribution with the appropriate scalar precision. 
This will avoid unnecessary matrix computations in computing the likelihood for `y`.

-Chris
